about: Trigger eval for skills/bouncer's description (PLAN.md 'The skill', gate: 90% or better each way for the new description). Each prompt was read against each description as a skill router would, with the skill's name visible. The first reading was self-judged; `routerRun` is skill-creator's description eval, run 2026-11-20. In each row, `old` and `new` say whether that description loads the skill for the prompt.

old.text: Turn a ticket or spec for one module (TypeScript, Python, Go or Rust), or for a change to one package of an existing TypeScript or Python repository, into a public test suite for the implementing agent and a calibrated hidden suite that judges its work, with the spec's decisions confirmed by a person before any test is written. Use when someone wants agent-written code accepted by tests the agent never saw, wants to grade an agent's submission against a spec, or wants to stop trusting an agent's own green test run.

new.text: Use when an agent says it's done or that the tests pass and the person doubts it: "check my agent's work", "is this really done", "bounce this", "I don't trust its green tests", "did it game the tests". Also for grading a contractor's, candidate's or agent's submission against a spec or ticket, and for tests an agent can't see for a ticket. Bouncer turns the ticket into a spec the person confirms, a public suite for the implementing agent and a calibrated hidden suite he keeps, then judges the work: passed, overfit, incomplete, regressed or refused. One module (TypeScript, Python, Go, Rust), a command, an HTTP service or one package of a TypeScript or Python repository. Not for writing ordinary unit tests, raising coverage, fixing a failing test, or a code, style or security review by eye.
